newsitem.title: UK: LDC debt glides calmly to close after bumper year.
newsitem.headline: LDC debt glides calmly to close after bumper year.

text.p: Emerging debt prices glided calmly into the last trading session of 1996 on Tuesday, with scarcely any activity to ruffle the waters after a successful trading year.
"There's literally been two or three trades," said one dealer at a European bank in London. "I can confirm there's nothing going on."
One dealer reported a little interest in Russia early in the London session, and in Bulgaria and Morocco later on.
"If anything a few bids are getting hit," the trader said, but added he expected prices to stay firm on the expectation of new money in January.
"I expect the market will be well bid for the next month," he said.
Russian dollar Vnesh loans were flat at 79-3/4. Bulgaria, still without a prime minister, is expected to get a new cabinet by mid-January. Still under pressure, its IABs shed 1/4 to 51-3/8.

Moroccan Series A paper eased 1/8 to 82-1/2 but volumes were minimal, and Latin paper was steady with Brazilian C bonds flat at 74-5/8. The JP Morgan composite Emerging Market Bond Index, updated after Monday's close of trade, was up nearly 40 percent at 143.73 over the year to December 30.

Russia was the year's biggest gainer, up a spectacular 113.09 percent. South Africa was the year's worst performer, climbing only 8.63 percent over the same period. --Caroline Brothers, London Newsroom +44 171 542 2734
